evals.prompt: commit, I fixed pier not propagating kubectl's exit code and refactored the exec helper to be cleaner while I was in there
evals.expected_output: The skill proposes 1 commit with type fix (not refactor), because fix triggers a release via svu and is the dominant type. The body captures both the exit-code fix and the refactoring rationale.
assertions: The commit type is fix (not refactor)
The commit body references both the exit-code fix and the exec-helper refactor
The skill does not split this into separate fix and refactor commits

evals.prompt: commit internal/kube/exec.go, internal/kube/exec_test.go, and README.md — the exec change adds a --dry-run passthrough and the README just fixes a typo
evals.expected_output: The skill proposes exactly 2 commits: one feat(kube) commit with exec.go and exec_test.go, and one docs commit for README.md. They are unrelated logical units.
assertions: One commit has scope kube and includes both exec.go and exec_test.go with type feat
The other commit is type docs for README.md
The README change is not bundled into the feat commit

evals.expected_output: If the current branch is develop or main (pier's protected branches), the skill blocks, suggests a feature branch named <type>/<description>, and waits before committing.
assertions: The skill checks the current branch before committing
If on develop or main, it blocks and does not commit directly
It suggests a feature branch following the <type>/<short-description> convention
It waits for the user's decision instead of proceeding automatically
